lead: Water dish with a rough outside and a smooth grey-brown bottom - it can be partly buried in the substrate to look like a natural pool.

description.html: This rustic water dish has two faces. The outside is rough, knobbly and uneven, like a broken-off piece of rock, while the inside is smooth, with grey-brown swirls that resemble a polished river stone. The water basin is deeper than in the shallow dishes in our range.

The rough outside allows a nice decorating trick: you can partly bury the dish in the substrate so only the uneven rim shows. It then looks like a pool between rocks rather than a dish sitting on the terrarium floor. The smooth bottom, on the other hand, makes washing easier because dirt does not get into pores.
The deeper basin suits adult lizards and snakes that drink larger amounts of water. For hatchlings and very small geckos, choose one of our shallower dishes.

Change the water every day. If the dish is buried, make sure substrate does not fall into the water; the rim should sit slightly above the substrate level. Once a week, take it out, wash it and put it back in the same spot.
